title: Security, Privacy, and Abuse Resistance

weeks.focus: Model and freeze assets, actors, trust boundaries, abuse cases, privacy flows, and residual risks
Build identity, session, authorization, tenant, credential, audit, deletion, and abuse controls
Break and measure nine security, privacy, supply-chain, abuse, and tool boundaries
evidence: Major threat model and verification report

weeks.focus: Decide, teach, assess, and remediate the security architecture

readiness_note: Ready on 2026-08-03 after isolated six-run calibration, deterministic lab checks, semantic review, and focused and full course validation.

outcomes.statement: Build a repeatable threat model from assets, actors, data flows, trust boundaries, abuse cases, risk owners, and reversal evidence.
Design identity, authentication, recovery, session binding, assurance, expiry, revocation, and replay controls.
Select role, attribute, or relationship authorization and enforce deny-by-default checks for every object and action.
Preserve tenant isolation and least privilege through data, cache, file, queue, search, administrative, and break-glass paths.
Operate scoped secrets, certificates, and encryption keys through issuance, rotation, revocation, recovery, and retirement without inventing cryptography.
Design attributable tamper-detectable audit evidence and verified classification, minimization, retention, deletion, residency, and backup handling.
Bound dependency, supply-chain, economic-abuse, prompt-injection, and tool-authorization risk with deterministic enforcement and security response.
Diagnose nine adversarial failures and defend a security architecture with residual risk, ownership, cost, migration, and reversal conditions.

resources.title: Threat Modeling Cheat Sheet
resources.purpose: Apply the four-question process to concrete assets, flows, boundaries, threats, and testable responses.
resources.assignment: Read Overview through Review and Validation; submit one data-flow boundary, three contextual threats, responses, owners, and validation tests.

resources.title: Application Security Verification Standard 5.0.0
resources.purpose: Turn threats into versioned verification requirements rather than generic control labels.
resources.assignment: Read What is ASVS and How to Reference Requirements; select and version five requirements that test the Northstar model, explaining exclusions.

resources.title: NIST SP 800-63B-4: Authentication and Authenticator Management
resources.author_or_publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
resources.purpose: Separate authentication assurance, authenticator lifecycle, recovery, and session continuity.
resources.assignment: Read Sections 2, 4, and 5; produce one assurance choice, recovery abuse case, session-binding contract, timeout, and revocation test.

resources.title: Authorization Cheat Sheet
resources.purpose: Design per-request, per-object, per-action authorization with explicit deny behavior and tests.
resources.assignment: Read all Recommendations; submit an allow/deny matrix and four negative regression tests, including policy failure behavior.

resources.title: Multi-Tenant Application Security Cheat Sheet
resources.purpose: Trace tenant identity through every shared data and execution surface.
resources.assignment: Read Key Risks, Best Practices, and Do's and Don'ts; audit API, database, cache, file, queue, search, and administrative paths.

resources.title: Zanzibar: Google's Consistent, Global Authorization System
resources.author_or_publisher: Ruoming Pang et al.; USENIX and Google
resources.type: open paper and recorded practitioner presentation
resources.purpose: Evaluate relationship authorization, consistency, caching, and centralized policy as operated-system trade-offs.
resources.assignment: Watch the presentation or read Sections 1-3 and 5-7 of the paper; record the data model, stale-decision risk, operating cost, and one simpler alternative.

resources.title: Secrets Management Cheat Sheet
resources.purpose: Design secret scope, custody, rotation, revocation, auditing, and exposure response.
resources.assignment: Read General Secrets Management, CI/CD, Detection, and Incident Response; create one lifecycle and rotation-without-outage experiment.

resources.title: NIST Key Management Guidelines
resources.author_or_publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
resources.purpose: Distinguish key material, cryptoperiods, protection, compromise, recovery, and destruction.
resources.assignment: Read the SP 800-57 Part 1 Rev. 5 overview and lifecycle guidance; map one key from generation through destruction and name its owner.

resources.title: Logging Cheat Sheet
resources.purpose: Make security events attributable and useful without logging secrets or unbounded sensitive data.
resources.assignment: Read Event Data Sources through Verification; define an audit event, prohibited fields, tamper signal, logging-failure test, retention, and access rule.

resources.title: NIST Privacy Framework 1.0
resources.author_or_publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
resources.purpose: Connect data processing, privacy outcomes, owners, and lifecycle verification without assuming one jurisdiction.
resources.assignment: Read the Framework Core Identify-P, Govern-P, Control-P, Communicate-P, and Protect-P outcomes; produce a data-action inventory and deletion exception register.

resources.title: SLSA Specification 1.2
resources.purpose: Separate provenance evidence from trust decisions and verify source/build expectations.
resources.assignment: Read About SLSA, Build Track Basics, Provenance, and Verifying Source; define one dependency acceptance policy and negative test.

resources.title: LLM Prompt Injection Prevention Cheat Sheet
resources.purpose: Treat instructions in retrieved content as adversarial data and preserve deterministic authorization.
resources.assignment: Read Common Attack Types, Primary Defenses, Agent-Specific Defenses, and Testing; submit one indirect-injection test and deterministic denial trace.

resources.title: AI Agent Security Cheat Sheet
resources.purpose: Bound tool identity, privilege, approvals, memory, budgets, audit, and recovery independently of model behavior.
resources.assignment: Read Threat Model, Least Privilege, Tool Authorization, Memory, Observability, and Adversarial Validation; produce a high-risk tool contract and failure matrix.

failure_experiments.scenario: cross-tenant object access through attacker-selected tenant context
failure_experiments.evidence: identity-bound tenant, requested/resource tenant, authorization decision, returned object count, denial audit, and I03-I04

failure_experiments.scenario: vertical privilege escalation on a high-risk object action
failure_experiments.evidence: subject role/attributes/relationships, object/action, policy version, enforcement point, deny result, and I02

failure_experiments.scenario: replayed, expired, or revoked session and credential
failure_experiments.evidence: authentication event, session age/binding, credential status, reauthentication/revocation result, audit, and I01

failure_experiments.scenario: exposed or over-scoped secret during rotation
failure_experiments.evidence: credential identity/scope/version, old/new acceptance windows, revocation, consumer rollout, recovery, and I05

failure_experiments.scenario: missing, sensitive, or tampered security audit evidence
failure_experiments.evidence: actor/action/object/outcome, prohibited fields, integrity link, access, tamper alert, logging failure, and I06

failure_experiments.scenario: deletion gap across authoritative data, cache, index, export, log, or backup
failure_experiments.evidence: data inventory, deletion request, copy status, exception/expiry, verification owner, rebuilt query, and I07

failure_experiments.scenario: dependency digest or provenance differs from approved expectations
failure_experiments.evidence: dependency identity, digest, provenance, policy, quarantine decision, rebuild/rollback, owner, and I08

failure_experiments.scenario: per-actor or per-tenant economic abuse bypasses one global limit
failure_experiments.evidence: actor/tenant identity, admitted/denied work, resource and cost units, fairness, alerts, recovery, and I09

failure_experiments.scenario: malicious retrieved instructions request an unauthorized high-risk tool
failure_experiments.evidence: untrusted source, original intent, proposed tool arguments, deterministic policy, approval/idempotency, denial audit, and I10-I11
